title: The bounded constructible localizing hull as an intersection
statement:
Let u be a universe, let $\Lambda$ be a condensed ring with a specified
monoid-object structure [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], and let $X$ be a scheme in universe u.
Write $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ for the pulled-back ring object
[sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and $D_X=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$
for its ordinary unbounded derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects;
def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal B_X$ be the object property of
bounded complexes with constructible cohomology [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible].
Define $\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal B_X)$ to be the intersection of all object
properties of $D_X$ which contain $\mathcal B_X$, are invariant under isomorphism,
are triangulated, and are closed under ambient coproducts indexed by types in
universe u+1. The associated category is the full subcategory on this property.
There is no derived-completeness condition. For the certified adic coefficient
families this is the bounded-constructible specialization of
[sk-def-localizing-closure].

source.place: Part (1): the two localizing hulls used to restrict proper direct image.

proof.text: Form the stated intersection. Its minimality, repleteness, zero, shift, triangle and coproduct closure follow by checking each property in every member of the intersection.
The ambient module category is Grothendieck abelian, so its derived category has the required coproducts. Closure under those coproducts gives coproducts in the full subcategory.

Apply countable-coproduct idempotent completeness inside the hull. For an ambient retraction of a hull object, split its idempotent inside the hull and identify the two splitting objects by the explicit composites of their splitting maps. Repleteness gives retract closure.
